candidates.title: Leg Curl Form Tips (DO THIS!)
candidates.description:
Leg Curl Form Tips

1) Adjust the Roller Pad: Position the pad just above your heels, resting on your Achilles tendon (between your heel and calf). Avoid placing it on your calves, as this reduces your range of motion.

2) Set the Lever: Start with your legs fully extended in the highest position you can comfortably manage. This setup ensures you maximize the range of motion.

3) Optimize the Seat Position: Sit upright (or lean slightly forward to place your hamstrings in a more stretched position). Avoid leaning backward, as this shortens the hamstring muscles (not ideal for hypertrophy).

4) Grip the Handles: Hold the handles firmly to maintain stability and proper posture during the exercise.

5) Keep Your Hips Down: Avoid lifting your butt off the seat during the curl. Doing so shifts tension away from the hamstrings and limits your range of motion.

candidates.description:
For machine setup, see my previous video on how to set up the seated leg curl. All the info is there.

I will walk you through how to perform the seated leg curl. So what you’re going to do with your hands is you’re going to anchor yourself into the seat because your hamstrings cross your hip, and you want to anchor your pelvis to make this end... heavier than... the end that’s moving...so I am going to pull myself into the seat.

Create an arch in my lower back, and let’s perform the 4-step rep.

Step 1: 
Tighten your hamstrings before you move. 

Step 2: 
Squeeze your hamstring so hard that your hamstrings pull your heel towards your rear. 

Step 3: 
Squeeze your hamstrings as hard as you can, holding the isometric at the end of the range... there are a lot of benefits here too.

Step 4: 
Use your hamstring to fight the load back to the starting position. 

It’s that simple, those 4 Steps.

✅ The PERFECT Seated Leg Curl Tips

1️⃣ Set the lower pad properly – Position it between your Achilles and lower calves (not on your heels).

2️⃣ Align your knees with the machine’s pivot point – This keeps tension on the hamstrings and protects your knees.

3️⃣ Keep your toes neutral or slightly up (dorsiflexed) – This helps bias the hamstrings instead of letting the calves take over.

4️⃣ Lock the thigh pad down firmly – It should press securely against your quads so you’re not lifting during reps.

5️⃣ Grip the handles hard – Stay stable and brace your core.

6️⃣ Curl ALL the way – Full range of motion. Don’t stop halfway.

7️⃣ Keep your glutes glued to the seat – If your butt lifts, the weight is too heavy.
